BiblicalUsage: Adithaim is a town named once, in the list of cities given to Judah in the lowland — between Sharaim and Gederah, in the Shephelah west of Jerusalem. It appears in no story and no battle; it is simply one of the towns that made up Judah's inheritance, marked on the map and then left alone; the place itself is covered in the Biblical Places collection.
TheologicalSignificance: A town named once carries no teaching of its own, and I won't invent one for it. Its place in the list is enough: the land God promised was divided town by town, and even the towns without stories belonged to His people.
